text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
EarnsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
OrdersTakeout(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeInDiningHall(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah(x) ::: x is Hannah.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → EarnsMoney(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school work in student jobs, then they need to earn money.
∀x (OrdersTakeout(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrdersTakeout(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People at Mary's school order takeout or enjoy dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school enjoy dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → SpendsTimeInDiningHall(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school enjoy dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends.
Hannah(H) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
WorksInStudentJobs(H) ::: Hannah works in student jobs on campus.
( EarnsMoney(H) → (¬PickyEater(H) ∧ EarnsMoney(H))) ::: If Hannah needs to earn money, then she is neither picky nor needs to earn money (i.e., she doesn't need to earn money).

Conclusion:
AtSchool(H) ∧ ¬PickyEater(H) ∧ SpendsTimeInDiningHall(H) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school, not a picky eater, and spends a lot of her time in the campus dining halls.
